description: Device labels (WIRE-CONTRACT-V4 section 12.7.1, plans/PX-W13.md section 2.1). Every SDK normalises the label it sends as `deviceName` (device-code sign-in, licence activation, registration), and the Worker normalises it again on receipt: (1) map U+0009-000D, U+0085, U+00A0, U+2028, U+2029 and U+3000 to U+0020; (2) delete U+0000-001F, U+007F-009F, U+061C, U+200B-200F, U+202A-202E, U+2060-2064, U+2066-2069 and U+FEFF; (3) collapse runs of U+0020 to one and trim both ends; (4) keep at most 64 code points (`DEVICE_LABEL_MAX_CODEPOINTS`; code points, never UTF-16 units) and trim a trailing space the cut exposes; (5) an empty result is no label: `expect: null`, the member is omitted and the Worker stores NULL. No Unicode normalisation; nothing is ever rejected. Each runner asserts its `normalizeDeviceLabel` maps every `raw` to `expect`. Non-ASCII code points are written escaped. Append-only: a new row keeps `deviceLabelVersion`; a changed row or rule bumps it.

cases.description: An ordinary ASCII label is unchanged.
Runs of spaces collapse to one; both ends are trimmed.
Step 1: tab, line feed, vertical tab, form feed and carriage return become spaces, then collapse.
Step 2: the C0 controls outside step 1 (here NUL, BEL and ESC) are deleted, not spaced.
Step 2: DEL and the C1 controls are deleted; NEL (U+0085) is whitespace and becomes a space first.
Step 1: NBSP and the ideographic space become spaces.
Step 1: U+2028 and U+2029 become spaces.
Step 2: the Arabic letter mark (U+061C) is deleted.
Step 2: zero-width space, non-joiner and joiner, and the LRM and RLM marks (U+200B-200F) are deleted.
Step 2: a right-to-left override that would render the tail reversed (`exe.png`) is deleted, so the label reads in logical order.
Step 2: the bidi embeddings, pop and overrides (U+202A-202E) are deleted.
Step 2: the word joiner and the invisible operators (U+2060-2064) are deleted.
Step 2: the bidi isolates (U+2066-2069) are deleted.
Step 2: a byte order mark (U+FEFF) is deleted.
Letters, punctuation and symbols outside the two lists are kept as they are.
There is no NFC step: a decomposed e and combining acute accent stay two code points.
Exactly 64 code points: kept whole.
65 code points: cut to the first 64.
An astral emoji as the 64th code point is kept whole: the limit counts code points (64 here), not UTF-16 units (65).
An astral emoji as the 65th code point is cut whole, never split into a lone surrogate.
Step 4 trims a trailing space the cut exposes: the 64th code point is a space.
The limit applies after steps 1-3: deleted code points and collapsed spaces do not count.

cases.description: Only whitespace: nothing is left, so the label is absent.
Only deleted code points: the label is absent.
The empty string is no label.
